title: Memphis Five at Healy's Balconnades; the Louisiana Five
summary: The Memphis Five played the popular Healy's Balconnades at 66th and Broadway. Kirkeby had nothing to do with the Louisiana Five and does not recall Anton Lada or Nunez.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: The Louisiana Five came along, too, in these later years. Yeah. That is, in the early 20s. They're late with respect to New Orleans jazz band. Did they work in the same idiom, same type of job?
Same type thing, yeah, sure. Same type thing. Philly, Napoleon, the gang, is Memphis Five. They worked up at the Healy's Balconnades. It was one of their jobs when I had them, you know.

66th and Broadway, yeah. Lincoln Square, I think they called it. And, uh, that was a very popular dance hall, you know. And, uh, they really, uh, tore up the place there on Friday, Saturday nights, you know. It was a terrific business.
Louisiana Five had some New Orleans men in it, at least at times.
Do you happen to remember anything about that?
I don't, I had nothing to do with Louisiana Five.
Don't recall. Do you remember the name of Lada, Anton Lada? He was a New Orleans boy who worked with them.

And I think Nunez was with Louisiana Five on some recording. I'm not sure of the history of those people in New York City. They were with Louisiana Five at times, and I haven't run down very much information. Do you remember the names of any other groups that were in this category generally?
